title: Turn a plugin into a light master (ESL) in the Creation Kit, and compact its Form IDs first
content:
Turn a plugin into a light master (ESL) in the Creation Kit, and compact its Form IDs first
Load your ESP as the active file, then File > Compact Active File Form IDs, save, then File > Convert Active File to Light Master. Compacting renumbers the Form IDs inside the plugin, so do it before converting and save the ESP afterwards. A light master holds at most 4096 forms (Form IDs 0x000-0xFFF; 2048 before game version 1.34) and loads in the shared 0xFE slot, so many ESLs fit in one load order. A modder's ESL must not use a normal ESP as a master. To edit an ESL again: rename the .esl to .esp (game/CK v1.10+), load it, and saving removes the light flag.

title: Precombines and previs in the Creation Kit: where the commands are
content:
Precombines and previs in the Creation Kit: where the commands are
Precombined meshes: World menu > PreCombine Geometry for Current Cell, for Loaded Area, For World, or For Interior Cells. Previs: Visibility menu > Generate Precombined Visibility for Current Cell, or for All Loaded Cells. The previs command works on the precombined meshes (hence its name), so run the PreCombine command first, then previs. The Visibility menu also has Generate Visibility for Current Cell / All Loaded Cells (the older, non-precombined visibility). In the Cell View window, right-click a cell > Update PreCombine/Previs Timestamp. Any edit to precombined references in a cell breaks that cell's precombines/previs until they are regenerated. For crashes while generating, see the CKPE entries (command-line generation).

title: Detect when items are added to or removed from a container in Papyrus (OnItemAdded / OnItemRemoved)
content:
Detect when items are added to or removed from a container in Papyrus (OnItemAdded / OnItemRemoved)
Put a script on the container (ObjectReference) and handle Event OnItemAdded and Event OnItemRemoved. These events are only sent after the script calls AddInventoryEventFilter(akFilter): no filter means no events. The filter can be a base object (exact match), a keyword, a component, a form list (only items in the list pass; nested lists are not searched), or None for every item - then the script must cope with hundreds of events at once. Each script on an object keeps its own filters; RemoveInventoryEventFilter and RemoveAllInventoryEventFilters remove them.

title: Navmesh floating in the air or buried after editing the landscape (terrain) in the Creation Kit, and how to fix it
content:
Navmesh floating in the air or buried after editing the landscape (terrain) in the Creation Kit, and how to fix it
Symptom: you raised, lowered or dug terrain (Landscape Editing, key H) - for example deepened a river or pond - and NPCs now walk on air, walk across water as if it were a floor, sink into the ground or get stuck. Cause: editing the landscape does NOT move the navmesh. It stays at the old ground height: where you dug down it floats (often right at the water surface), where you raised the ground it is buried. Vanilla navmeshes you never touched are affected too if the ground under them changed. If you also removed or added objects there, the old navmesh still has holes cut for objects that are gone and none for the new ones. Measured on a real mod that dug out a river near Sanctuary: 3,812 navmesh points off the new ground (typically 150-350 units, up to 666) in 22 cells.
Best fix (cells where the ground changed a lot or many objects were removed/added): rebuild the navmesh in your plugin, the same way you would for a new area. Plugin loaded as the active file, open the cell, Ctrl+E. Delete the old navmesh in that cell (select with T triangle mode and drag, then R or Delete). Then NavMesh > Generation > Recast-Based Generation with Include Landscape ticked, clean up by hand (delete islands and triangles on things nobody can stand on; I selects every navmesh except the selected one), NavMesh > Finalize Cell NavMeshes (joins it to the neighbouring cells), NavMesh > Check NavMeshes and fix what it lists, save. Vanilla navmesh records must NOT end up deleted: each one has to remain at least as a single triangle (see the entry on keeping vanilla navmesh records) - check the saved plugin in xEdit for deleted NAVM records before release.
Quick touch-up (cells only slightly off, e.g. 50-100 units, no objects changed): V vertex mode, drag-select the floating vertices over the edited ground (not ones on bridges, rocks or buildings), press F to drop them to the ground; buried vertices: hold Z and drag them up above the ground first, then F. Then Finalize Cell NavMeshes. Navmesh on a river bottom is correct - vanilla does it.

title: Creation Kit navmesh editing keys, menus and dialogs in Fallout 4
content:
Creation Kit navmesh editing keys, menus and dialogs in Fallout 4
Ctrl+E turns navmesh editing on/off. The Fallout 4 CK's own NavMesh Quick Help lists: T triangle selection mode, V vertex selection mode, G edge selection mode, D deselect, R or Delete delete the selection, F flood fill / drop vertices (with vertices selected it drops them to the ground; with a triangle selected it selects everything connected to it), A create a triangle from 3 selected vertices, Q or M merge vertices, S rotate (flip) an edge, E edit cover on an edge, O toggle preferred-pathing triangle, W toggle the view normal / transparent / navmesh only, N toggle draw-mode grid 5x5 / 1x1, C centre on the selection, Z (held) Z-plane movement, Ctrl+Z undo. Building by hand (from Bethesda's navmesh tutorial for the same editor): right-click the ground to place a vertex, Ctrl+right-click with two vertices selected adds a triangle, Tab swaps which two stay selected, double-click an edge then Ctrl+double-click another edge to fill between them, I selects every navmesh except the selected one (handy for deleting islands). NavMesh menu: Generation (Havok-Based, Recast-Based, Advanced), Auto Generate WorldSpace, Check NavMeshes, Finalize Cell NavMeshes, Find Cover Edges, precut tools for scrappable objects, Move Selection To Separate NavMesh, Navmesh Draw Mode, Draw Cover, Remove Cell NavMeshes, Finalize Loaded Area / WorldSpace / All Interiors, Select Triangle By Index, Export Navmesh as OBJ, pathing tests. A triangle's type can be Normal, Water, Door, Preferred, NoLargeCreature or Float. The Recast Navmesh Generation dialog has Include Landscape, Agent Height, Agent Max Climb, Agent Low/High Slope and Generate Float Navmesh. The Select Triangle dialog (Check NavMeshes) steps through warnings (Next Warning, Delete Warning Triangle, Try AutoFix, Re-Check NavMesh).

title: Removing and rebuilding navmesh in a vanilla exterior cell: keep every vanilla navmesh record (at least one triangle)
content:
Removing and rebuilding navmesh in a vanilla exterior cell: keep every vanilla navmesh record (at least one triangle)
Removing a vanilla area's navmesh and generating new navmesh in your own plugin is a normal way to redo an area you changed. The one rule: vanilla navmesh records (Form IDs starting 00 in Fallout4.esm) are linked to their neighbours and listed in the worldspace's navmesh info, so a vanilla NAVM record must never end up DELETED in your plugin - LOOT and xEdit flag 'deleted navmeshes' as a crash risk and they cannot be cleaned automatically. What must remain is the record, not its old shape: a vanilla navmesh cut down to a single triangle is fine. Bethesda does this itself (Fallout4.esm has 406 navmeshes that are one triangle, left where they are), and a real Sanctuary mod that rebuilt its cells this way ended with 37 vanilla records as one-triangle stubs, new navmesh in its own records, and 0 deleted records. So: before generating, if needed delete all but one triangle of each vanilla navmesh in the cell; after saving, open the plugin in xEdit and confirm no NAVM record is marked deleted. Automatic generation replaces the navmesh in the area it works on (Bethesda's tutorial: select references with Ctrl+Alt+drag first to generate without deleting the other navmeshes), which is why the check after saving matters.

title: Should navmesh go under water (river and pond beds)? What vanilla Fallout 4 does
content:
Should navmesh go under water (river and pond beds)? What vanilla Fallout 4 does
Yes. Fallout 4 puts navmesh on the bottom of rivers and ponds: around Sanctuary (exterior grid x -30..-10, y 10..30) 11,623 vanilla navmesh triangles lie more than 30 units under the water surface; vanilla navmesh points under water are typically 62 units deep, 90% within 424 and the deepest 1,269. Those underwater triangles carry the same flags as dry ones, so nothing special is needed. So when you deepen a river, the navmesh belongs on the new riverbed - drop it there - not at the water surface. Slopes: vanilla navmesh there is often steep (median 14 degrees, 10% steeper than 45, 8% steeper than 50), so a riverbank that comes out steep after dropping the vertices is normal; only delete triangles that run up a near-vertical face.
